City of Deltona Ordinance, SEC. 18-5 IPMC 304.7 - Housing Code Roofs - 
Violation: City of Deltona Ordinance, Section 18-5, which adopts the latest edition of the International Property Maintenance Code, Section 304.7, which states the roof and slashing shall be sound tight and not have any defects that admit rain. 

Corrective Action:
Repair or replace the roof, gutters, or drainage. Contact our office with permit number when obtained. 

The case for this violation was opened on February 7, 2022. On July 27, 2022 the Special Magistrate found the Respondent in violation of the City Code and based on the evidence, the time provided to comply in the prior Order of February 7,2022, was sufficient to fully correct the violation. A total fine in the amount of $60,800.00 representing three hundred and four days (304) non-compliance at a rate of $200.00 per day was imposed.

• Amends Ch. 651 (Expedited Permitting) to revise the eligibility criteria for the expedited permitting process, designate the Public Works Department as responsible for coordination and implementation, and establish fees
• Establishes an initial Expedited Permitting Program Fee of $20,000, which may be increased up to $40,000 by the Director of Public Works without Council approval
• Establishes an Exceptional Project Fee, which cannot exceed 200% of the Expedited Permitting Program Fee without approval of the Chief Administrative Officer, for projects based on size, complexity, number of structures or permits, number of required reviewing agencies, phased permitting requirements, or other characteristics requiring greater resources, to be paid in addition to the Expedited Permitting Program Fee
• These fees are supplemental and will not replace, reduce, credit against, or otherwise affect any other fees that are applicable to any project
• The Expedited Permitting Program Fee and Exceptional Project Fee will be deposited as follows: 90% to the Building Inspection Fund and 10% to the Affordable Housing Special Revenue Fund

• NFSSE will use the funding to repair a walking and running track on their campus, pay a portion of the salaries for a physical education teacher, health and fitness coach, and fitness coordinator, and to purchase athletic equipment to support various physical education programs
